issues.description: The UML in the problem statement specifies getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor() should return a double (problem_statement.md shows +getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor(): double), but the solution implementation declares and returns an int (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java: lines 84-87). This not only mismatches the expected return type but also causes integer division (losing fractional students per tutor). The template contains a TODO for this method (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) and therefore students following the UML would implement a double, while the solution demonstrates an int — a cross-artifact type/signature inconsistency that can cause confusion and test failures.
issues.suggested_fix: Update the solution to match the UML and problem description: change the method signature to public double getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor() and compute using floating point division, e.g. return (double) getTotalNumberOfStudents() / getNumberOfTutors(); (optionally handle the case of zero tutors to avoid division by zero). This keeps the template, problem statement and solution consistent.
